title: Rank of an integral closure over a principal ideal domain
statement: Let $A$ be a principal ideal domain with fraction field $K$, and let $L/K$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $C$ be a commutative $A$-algebra embedded in $L$, with both structural maps $A\to L$ equal to the composite through $K$ and through $C$, and suppose $C$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $\operatorname{finrank}_A C=\dim_K L$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Here the rank of the finite free $A$-module $C$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] is the cardinality of any basis.

proof.text: A PID is Noetherian and integrally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] makes $C$ finite over $A$. It is torsion-free since it embeds in the field $L$ and nonzero elements of $A$ stay nonzero there. The PID form of [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes it free. Localizing an $A$-basis of $C$ at the nonzero elements of $A$ gives a $K$-basis of $L$: every $z\in L$ has an integral nonzero multiple $az\in C$, and every finite $K$-linear relation can be multiplied by a common nonzero denominator to give an $A$-linear relation. Thus the two basis cardinalities agree, giving the equality by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. This is exactly IsIntegralClosure.rank, whose proof uses IsIntegralClosure.isLocalization and Basis.localizationLocalization; its source and all hypotheses were checked in the pinned Mathlib.
